title: Chapter 90: The Cursed Ballpoint Pen
html:
Fan Yu’s aunt had seen the classroom too. The children at the desks sat with bowed heads, just like the students in her brother’s group photograph. Terror froze her face as she collapsed. She tried to rise, but her limbs would not obey.

“Shh!” Chen Ge rushed to her side, seized her arm, and half dragged her from the education block.

The rumors were real. Regardless of their cause of death, the students had all returned to that classroom.

“You saw them, didn’t you? You saw them!” A photograph was one thing; seeing the students in person was another. The woman’s eyes bulged, and every breath came in a ragged gasp.

“Let’s get out of here first.” Chen Ge dragged Fan Yu’s aunt toward the entrance. Before leaving, he glanced back. The classroom door and windows were closed, and beyond them lay perfect darkness.

I’ve been in the school this long, and they haven’t tried to attack me. They probably aren’t malevolent spirits.There was evidence for that conclusion. The girl Fan Yu’s father had driven insane committed suicide in that classroom, and one of its spirits had emerged to help her. The spirits had also written the warning notes to Fan Yu’s father. They had tried to protect the school’s students, even if their methods were misguided.

Supporting Fan Yu’s aunt, Chen Ge made his way to Mu Yang High School’s front gate, where they sheltered from the rain. It was already past midnight. Remaining inside the three buildings seemed unwise, especially with Fan Yu’s aunt as an unpredictable liability.

Around one in the morning, the rain began to ease. A light approached the school. Chen Ge switched on his flashlight and shouted for help. Leaves parted in the forest as a group in raincoats forced their way through.

“Here! The suspect has already been detained!” Chen Ge was excited, but when he saw the person who was leading the way, his confidence dwindled.

“Why is it you again?” Inspector Lee’s face twitched when he reached the gate and saw Chen Ge. “The same person has called the emergency line three times in one week. In thirty-five years, that has never happened at our station. Did you know that? The dispatcher says he recognizes your voice now.”

Chen Ge had no answer. Embarrassed, he hauled Fan Yu’s aunt to her feet and led her over. Inspector Lee ordered his men to break open the school gate, then asked, “Is she another victim?”

“No, she’s one of the killers.” Chen Ge handed Fan Yu’s aunt over to one of the officers.

“One of them?” Inspector Lee flashed his light three times to alert his men. “Is another killer still hiding inside the school?”

“The other one is dead.” Chen Ge summarized what he knew. “Her brother was a voyeur. When his wife found out, she used the secret to force a divorce. He refused to let her go and killed her instead. This woman witnessed the murder, then killed her brother before he could kill her.”

“Self-defense?” Inspector Lee immediately seized on the crucial point.

“If it was, she should have called the police. Instead, she cleaned up the scene and left. The murders happened three years ago, and there are no other witnesses. Everything I know came from her.” Chen Ge pointed at Fan Yu’s aunt. “She could be lying.”

“Where is the crime scene?” Inspector Lee did not even bother asking why Chen Ge was there. His fellow officers took Chen Ge’s presence in stride as well.

“You’ll have to ask her.” Chen Ge wanted the well’s location too; it was the last of his four side missions. Inspector Lee was a far more experienced interrogator. He took a clean towel from one of his men and offered it to Fan Yu’s aunt. “Attempted murder can carry the death penalty, but if you acted in self-defense and show genuine remorse, you might still see the outside of a prison again.”

Fan Yu’s aunt gripped the towel silently. She did not look particularly afraid of death.

“Think about your family. At your age, you must have children of your own. If you refuse to cooperate, you may never see them again.” Inspector Lee found the opening he needed. At once, Fan Yu’s aunt began to waver.

After another ten minutes of persuasion, she finally spoke. “They’re buried on the hill behind the school, but I only remember the general area.”

She led Chen Ge and the police to a small hill behind the school. “The bodies were thrown into a well. A landslide buried it completely.”

No road near Mu Yang High School could accommodate heavy machinery, so finding the well would require digging by hand. Chen Ge had already considered that.

“Inspector Lee, if we don’t verify her story now, things might change after dawn.” Chen Ge squeezed in beside him, anxious about his final side mission.

“We’ll secure the scene and wait for a crew with the proper tools before we start digging.” Inspector Lee was already on the phone making arrangements; he needed no reminder from Chen Ge.

The crew finally arrived at 2:15 am. Inspector Lee assigned the work, and the digging began in earnest. Chen Ge seized a shovel and joined them with such dedication that the officers were genuinely moved.

At three, the buried well finally emerged. At 4:30, they broke it open and recovered two bodies.

At that moment, Chen Ge’s black phone vibrated with a mission-completion notice.

He set down his shovel, found a secluded spot, and opened the message.

“You reached the Mission Location on time, experienced all four side missions, and survived until dawn. Mu Yang High School Trial Mission completed! A new scenario has been unlocked. The player may freely control the set’s props through the phone interface!

“Trial Mission completion rate exceeds ninety percent. Hidden mission item unlocked—The Cursed Ballpoint Pen.

“The Cursed Ballpoint Pen (Broken): The Pen Spirit refused to answer your summons. It rolled its eyes at you and hid.”
